text: This is OmniOffloader, a free WordPress plugin that moves your media library to cloud storage, serves it from your own CDN, and lets you bring it all back anytime. In this walkthrough, we'll install it, connect a bucket, and go through every feature, one by one.

OmniOffloader is free in the WordPress.org plugin directory. The plugin page lists every supported provider and feature, and links to the full documentation, with step-by-step guides for each provider.
To install it, open Plugins, Add New Plugin, and search for OmniOffloader. Click Install Now, then Activate. Prefer the terminal? One WP-CLI command installs and activates it.
After activation, OmniOffloader appears in your admin menu, with five screens: Dashboard, Settings, Offload, Bring Back, and Tools. Nothing is uploaded anywhere until you connect a storage provider.

Open Settings and choose your provider: Amazon S3, Cloudflare R2, DigitalOcean Spaces, Backblaze B2, Wasabi, or any S3-compatible storage. Enter your access key, secret and bucket name, then click Test Connection. When you see Connected, you're ready. You can also keep your keys out of the database, by defining them in wp-config.php.

Next, serving media from your CDN. Enter your custom domain: the public address that serves your bucket, like media.yourdomain.com. Most buckets aren't public by default, and Cloudflare R2 has no public address until you connect a custom domain, or turn on its r2.dev URL. Once media is offloaded, URLs are rewritten as your pages render: images, srcset, galleries, video and audio. Nothing in your database is changed.

Not ready to switch yet? With Retain Local Files, turn off Serve Media from Cloud. Your media is still offloaded as a backup, but your site keeps loading it from your own server. When your CDN is ready, turn it back on and save, and every page switches right away. Just clear your page cache afterwards.

Now choose a retention policy. Retain Local Files keeps everything on your server, and it's the safest place to start. Smart Local Cleanup deletes the generated thumbnails, and keeps your originals. Full Cloud Migration removes every local copy, to free the most disk space. A local file is never deleted until its upload is confirmed in your bucket.

Under Behavior, Background Cloud Offload keeps your uploads fast. Transfer Speed sets how many files move at once: Low for small shared hosting, Balanced for most sites, and Fast or Custom for a VPS. Mirror Delete removes the cloud copy when you delete media in WordPress. A custom path prefix stores your files in a folder of your choice, and Object Versioning stops CDN caches from serving stale files. Then click Save changes.

From now on, every new upload is offloaded automatically, in the background: the original, every thumbnail, the scaled version, and WebP or AVIF sources. In the Media Library, the status changes from Queued to Offloaded.

For the media you already have, open the Offload page. It shows your total media, what's already offloaded, and what's still local. Choose All Local Media, or a custom amount, to try a small batch first. Click Start Bulk Offload, and watch the progress bar and the live activity log. The job runs in the background, so you can leave the page, and Cancel stops it at any time.

Have a large library, five thousand items or more? We recommend WP-CLI. There's no browser and no web time limit, and with the concurrency option it uploads up to sixty-four files at once. Start it in the background, watch its log, and check the speed and time left with the status command. While it runs, the admin screens show its progress too. Stop it anytime with the stop command, then run the same command again to continue where it left off.

The Media Library shows the offload status of every file, and you can filter by offloaded or local only. Each row has Offload now or Bring Back actions, and the bulk actions menu handles up to a thousand selected files. When you edit an attachment, the OmniOffloader box shows where it's stored, with one-click buttons.

Bring Back reverses everything. Open the Bring Back page and check the preflight: the estimated download, and your free disk space. Choose all media or a custom amount. Keep Cloud Copies is recommended, and deleting from the cloud only happens after every file is verified on your server. Click Start Bring Back, and follow the progress. Using a cleanup policy? Always run Bring Back before you deactivate the plugin. And for a large library, use the restore command in WP-CLI.

On the Tools page, apply a new retention policy to media you already offloaded. Before any local copy is deleted, every file is checked in the cloud, by size. Changed your path prefix? Move Media copies older files into the current folder, right inside your bucket, so nothing is downloaded.

Copying your site to staging, or to your own computer? Safe Mode detects the copy, and blocks every upload and delete, so it never touches your live bucket, while your media keeps loading. Several sites can also share one bucket, each safely in its own folder.

Finally, the full WP-CLI reference is on the Tools screen, with examples and copy buttons, for offload, restore, retention, move, status and stop. Every command that changes something supports a dry run first.
That's OmniOffloader. Install it free from WordPress.org, and find every guide at omnioffloader dot vercel dot app.
